newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees '98 central gvt deficit at 2.0 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees '98 central gvt deficit at 2.0 pct/GDP.

text.p: Spain's budget draft for 1998 sets a target for the central government deficit of 2.0 percent of GDP, and a target for the public sector deficit of 2.4 percent of GDP, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

"Within the boundaries of austerity, the forecast for the (central government) deficit for 1998 will be two percent .. and the public sector deficit will be 2.4 percent," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told a news conference after the regular weekly Cabinet meeting.
Rodriguez said the cabinet had made a preliminary study of the broader figures for the 1998 budget on Thursday.
Rodriguez reiterated that the new budget draft did not include any tax hikes for 1998 and the government would try to improve the wellbeing of the people.
"In this budget the Spanish government will make an effort to improve Spanish welfare," Rodriguez said.

"(The budget) does not include tax rises in 1998, and includes great efforts to increase financing in a few areas -- for more jobs, aids for the mining sector, health, education, wage increases for public servants and public investment," he added.
Rodriguez said additional funds would be available thanks to savings in financial expenditure allowed by the rigorous fiscal policy followed by the government so far.
